shortlist.format: animation (standard player) plus a playable shootout block
shortlist.pitch_es: Un cobro de penal es un juego de suma cero: el cobrador elige palo natural, centro o palo contrario y el arquero elige hacia dónde lanzarse. La animación muestra cómo dos jugadores que juegan una y otra vez se acercan despacio al equilibrio, o dan vueltas para siempre, según la regla de aprendizaje que elijas, mientras el método símplex lo encuentra exacto en unos pocos pivotes. Al final ves que la mezcla óptima del cobrador son los precios sombra del PL del arquero divididos por su suma. Debajo cobras tú 15 penales contra un arquero que aprende de ti y descubres que solo la mezcla minimax te garantiza el 81,5 % contra cualquier arquero.
shortlist.optimization_es: Cada jugador resuelve un PL (el cobrador maximiza el gol que se garantiza contra cualquier lanzada y el arquero minimiza el que concede) y los dos PL son duales entre sí, así que el teorema minimax es dualidad fuerte, y el juego ficticio y los pesos multiplicativos son métodos iterativos cuyas cotas encierran el valor.
shortlist.effort: L (M without the shootout block; if scope must shrink, drop Hedge first, then the shootout)
shortlist.strengths: Highest mean score (9.0) and the best classroom fit: the minimax theorem appears as strong LP duality, the kicker's optimal mix is read from the keeper LP's shadow prices (builds directly on the Shadow Prices resource), complementary slackness becomes visible, and a 3x3 matrix lets students pivot by hand. Universal hook in Colombia. Only candidate with mixed strategies, a zero-sum game, the minimax theorem and an algorithm that plays against the visitor; Price Wars only has pure equilibria in continuous quantities. Core numbers verified with HiGHS and with the site's lp.js: v 81.53%, kicker (32.46, 15.74, 51.80)%, keeper (35.79, 16.89, 47.32)%, pure security levels 69.9% and 92.9%. Weak center reduces to a 2x2 natural/opposite game whose shares (38.5%, 42.0%) match Palacios-Huerta's minimax frequencies, a strong honesty anchor once checked against the paper.
shortlist.risks: Dense: two strategy triangles, three learning rules and a 15-kick game; teacher and visitor both ask to trim (drop Hedge before the shootout) and the visitor wants the shootout up front. Presets must stay away from support-change thresholds (a center value near 0.80 gives a 0.7% keeper stay that looks like a bug). Pivot counts and bounds depend on LP.steps (Dantzig rule), so they must never be hard-coded. 15 kicks are noise: never judge the visitor on realized goals. Overlap: Courier Wars (zero-sum LP with closing bounds) and Rangers (opponent indifference); this page owns the minimax theorem, LP duality, shadow prices and learning dynamics. Keep the band strip visually distinct from the primal-dual gap of lab-svm-dual and do not reuse the Price Wars staircase.
shortlist.corrections: (1) LP.steps uses Dantzig's rule (LP.solve uses Bland's). Reference upper bounds are 92.90, 92.00, 81.53 (not 90.2). Pivots: 3 Reference, 3 Panenka, 2 Weak center; the chip reads steps.length minus 1 from LP.steps, never r.iterations from LP.solve; never write 'three pivots' as a general fact. (2) Complementary slackness: a shot outside the support scores AT MOST v ('here strictly less'), not strictly less as a theorem. (3) The starting vertex w = 0 is not a keeper mix: show the pure minimax 92.9% there. (4) Per-pivot floors from the dual estimate are not monotone (69.9, 30.0, 81.5): draw the best floor so far starting at the pure maximin 69.9%, and explain that the primal simplex gives no useful floor until the last tableau, where dual feasibility closes the gap at once. (5) Hedge: the last iterate drifts away from the interior equilibrium (Bailey and Piliouras 2018, add to refs); only time averages converge; state the step rule on the page (recommended anytime eta_t = sqrt(8 ln 3 / t); fixed eta gives a wide early band 75.8 to 85.1 at t = 100). (6) Fictitious play: fix one variant (simultaneous, from the pure security strategies, ties to the lowest index; gives 80.97 to 82.01 at t = 1000 and 81.28 to 81.83 at t = 3000), read every band live, note the band of the current averages is not monotone, and claim no rate (Robinson 1951; Daskalakis and Pan 2014). (7) 'Every shot scores 81.5% against Minimax' holds only with full support (Reference, Panenka); in Weak center a center kick scores 75.0% < 79.6%. Wording: 'every shot in the mix scores v; a shot outside it scores less'. (8) Replace 'against the learners any imbalance costs you' with 'learners punish predictable patterns; only the minimax mix guarantees v against every keeper; 15 kicks prove nothing'. (9) 'Equilibrium where the three regions meet' only for Reference and Panenka; Weak center lies on the edge x_C = 0 on the N/O boundary; generate labels from the computed supports. (10) Spanish card: 'jugando una y otra vez', not 'a punta de ensayo y error'; shadow prices 'divididos por su suma'. (11) Cross-check tolerance 1e-6, since lp.js rounds outputs to 1e-9. (12) Pattern hunter uses order-1 transition counts (order 2 is almost always in fallback over 15 kicks).

shortlist.title_es: El atajo que nos atrasa a todos
shortlist.format: animation (standard player) plus a planner simulation block
shortlist.pitch_es: Abren un conector de dos minutos entre los dos corredores que llevan del norte al centro de una Bogotá estilizada, cada conductor toma la ruta que le conviene y, con 4.000 carros por hora, todos terminan llegando 18 minutos más tarde. La animación muestra que ese equilibrio de Wardrop es el mínimo de un programa convexo, el de Beckmann, que no es el tiempo total que le importa a la ciudad, y mide la distancia entre los dos con el precio de la anarquía. Con un control eliges la demanda de la mañana y ves cuándo el atajo ayuda, cuándo perjudica y cuándo nadie lo usa. Debajo juegas de planeador: abres o cierras el conector, pones peajes y un PL te da el peaje que menos recauda y aun así lleva a los conductores al óptimo del sistema.
shortlist.optimization_es: El equilibrio de Wardrop es el óptimo de un programa convexo (el de Beckmann) cuyas condiciones KKT dicen que toda ruta usada tarda lo mínimo, el óptimo del sistema minimiza el tiempo total con otro programa convexo, y entre todos los peajes que llevan al óptimo el que menos recauda se encuentra con un PL.
shortlist.effort: M (drop Frank-Wolfe from the animation and the 'Commute twelve mornings' mini game)
shortlist.strengths: Instantly shareable paradox in a context every student lives. Numbers verified in closed form, in Python and with lp.js: at 4,000 cars/h the connector moves the equilibrium from 2,000 + 2,000 at 70 min to 200 / 200 / 3,600 at 88 min (4,667 to 5,867 vehicle-hours), the optimum leaves the connector empty, price of anarchy 1.257 < 4/3; at 2,000 the connector helps (60 to 52 min); at 8,000 nobody uses it (zigzag 92 > 90); paradox window 2,533 to 7,600. Shows the contrast between what drivers minimize (a potential nobody pays) and what the city minimizes. The least-revenue toll LP is a ready class assignment. Unique equilibrium in path flows, tiny network, effort M. Nothing on the site about network equilibrium, Braess or price of anarchy; a cousin of Partes justas (price of fairness) without duplicating it.
shortlist.risks: Particles must be a pure function of t with speeds consistent with the minutes shown. The chapter story differs by scenario (helps, hurts, ignored), so it needs scenario-specific keys. 'A toll fixes it' is only true for travel time with toll money treated as a transfer. Strong overlap with Pricing the Road (roads, Wardrop followers, tolls) if both are built: then this page keeps congestion, price of anarchy and first-best tolls only. Fixed 45 min ring links are an idealization; keep the network stylized with no real road names.
shortlist.corrections: (1) Tolls fix total TRAVEL time only, with tolls treated as transfers returned to the city; drivers' time plus toll gets worse (4,000: marginal-cost tolls give 90 min per driver vs 88 untolled; 2,000: 88 vs 52, and the least-revenue toll 69 vs 52 to save 0.1 min of average travel time). Say so and show a 'time + toll per driver' chip. (2) At 4,000 the least-revenue toll is '18 minutes or more' on the connector (a ray of optima that all collect 0; LP.solve returns the vertex 18); at 2,000 the 19 min connector toll is unique (34,200 car-min/h vs 72,200 for marginal-cost tolls 19 + 19). Useful identity: revenue = d·pi minus total time at x*. (3) Chapters 3, 4 and 6 need scenario keys: hurt 'Everyone arrives later' (4,000), help 'Everyone arrives sooner' (2,000; the crowd passes the optimum 51.9 and ends at 52), idle 'Nobody takes it' (8,000: 0 rounds, PoA 1, least-revenue toll 0, marginal-cost tolls 40 + 40 collect 320,000 for no gain); chapter 6 'Tolls close the gap' or 'No toll needed'. (4) Gradient projection with damping 0.5 takes 11 rounds at 4,000, 1 at 2,000, 0 at 8,000 (not '10 to 20'); interpolate rounds over a fixed time span; the undamped Newton step lands in one round. (5) The worst demand is 3,800 cars/h (88 vs 69 min, ratio 1.2754), not 4,000; say 'worst' only if found live. (6) Find the window by bisection on the sign of E_open minus E_closed (lower end) and on f3 > 0 (upper end), since the difference is identically 0 above 7,600. (7) Label 'Time per driver' as an average (at the 2,000 optimum 200 drivers take 69 min and 1,800 take 50). (8) Frank-Wolfe only in a step note (fast at 4,000, slow tail at 8,000); MSA over 12 mornings does not reach equilibrium, so drop the mini game or never claim it does. (9) Card wording: 'el peaje que menos recauda' instead of 'el peaje más barato', and '18 minutos más tarde' always with 'con 4.000 carros por hora'.

shortlist.pitch_es: Tres equipos de guardaparques deben proteger ocho zonas de un parque ilustrativo del piedemonte amazónico contra taladores ilegales que observan las patrullas antes de cortar. Tú fijas con qué frecuencia se patrulla cada zona, los taladores van a la zona que más les conviene y ves cuántas hectáreas se afectan; las patrullas fijas o repartidas por igual salen mal. Luego la página calcula el patrullaje aleatorio óptimo con un PL por cada zona que podría ser atacada, lo confirma con un llenado de agua y sortea un día concreto de patrulla. Descubres que el mejor patrullaje deja a los taladores indiferentes entre varias zonas y que las hectáreas solo deciden hacia cuál de ellas los empujas, por eso el desempate importa tanto.
shortlist.optimization_es: Los guardaparques se comprometen con una cobertura aleatoria y la mejor respuesta de los taladores entra como restricciones lineales: se resuelve un PL por cada zona candidata y se queda el mejor factible (equivalente a un MILP con la elección binaria del atacante), y el llenado de agua confirma que esa cobertura minimiza la mejor ganancia esperada de los taladores.
shortlist.strengths: Effort M and numerically robust: every number reproduced with lp.js (3 teams: coverage (59.20, 51.65, 47.59, 42.60, 38.58, 29.14, 22.65, 8.59)%, water level 25.27, 8.16 ha; 2 teams 9.76 ha with Z8 unpatrolled and its LP correctly infeasible; 4 teams 6.76 ha); 8 LPs solve in 0.6 ms. Clear game loop with an emotional Colombian context (Amazon foothills deforestation). Teaches what Price Wars does not: Stackelberg commitment to a MIXED strategy against a discrete follower, solved by multiple LPs, plus how a mixed strategy becomes a concrete day (comb sampling). Every predictable plan loses (best deterministic patrol 20 ha; uniform 12.5; top timber 60). The tie-breaking lesson, well explained, is real security-games knowledge.
shortlist.risks: Knife-edge tie-breaking: rounding the optimum to 3 decimals sends the loggers to Z2 (21.78 ha) and ties against the rangers give 35.43 ha, which can look like a bug unless the page explains it. The visitor's slider grid cannot reach the optimum exactly. Overlap with the penalty page (indifference, mixed strategy, and here the coverage is the minimax of the loggers' payoffs) and with Courier Wars (units over map zones): keep the focus on commitment, tie-breaking and sampling, and avoid a zone-map look for Courier Wars. Avoid 'route' wording (Patrol Route is a TSP resource). No armed groups or real people.
shortlist.corrections: (1) Not 'general-sum, so not a plain minimax': every feasible LP returns the SAME coverage, the ORIGAMI vector that minimizes the loggers' best expected payoff (Korzhyk et al. 2011); hectares only choose which tied zone the loggers are steered to. The 8 LP mini cards show 8 objective values for one shared patrol, not 8 patrols. (2) 'Steers them to the least harmful zone' holds only under ranger-favorable tie-breaking; add a tie-breaking box with live numbers: ties to rangers 8.16 ha, ties against them 35.43 (2 teams 43.66, 4 teams 28.26), margin-robust LP with delta = 1 million COP 8.28 (9.88, 6.88) where Z1 is the strict best response, optimum rounded to 3 decimals sends loggers to Z2 (21.78). (3) One evaluation rule everywhere: exact ties at relative tolerance 1e-9, resolved for the rangers (a loose tolerance lets the visitor beat the optimum: tol 0.5 gives 8.10 < 8.16). (4) The 'you vs optimum' chip also shows the best reachable on the slider grid, computed live (1% steps: 10.0, 8.4, 7.0 ha). (5) Comb sampling: normalize sum c to m (the LP returns 2.999999999); add an idle segment when the visitor's sum is below m; the replay matches coverage only up to sampling noise (about plus or minus 7 points at 2 SD over 200 days), so use 365 days or more with a 2 SD band; say the loggers know c but not the day's draw. (6) Attribution: compact coverage LPs and the single-type MILP are ERASER (Kiekintveld et al. 2009); DOBSS (Paruchuri et al. 2008) is the Bayesian normal-form MILP; Conitzer and Sandholm (2006) is the multiple-LPs idea; implementability is Korzhyk, Conitzer and Parr (2010); comb sampling is systematic sampling (Madow 1949). (7) Plausibility: scale logger payoffs to tens of millions of COP and say 'hectares affected' (scaling changes neither the coverage nor the attacked zone).
shortlist.build_plan: Page site/lab/rangers-move-first.html, bundles site/locales/lab/lab-patrols.{en,es,pt,fr}.js, prefix pat; eyebrow 'Lab · Proposal · Game' (Juego / Jogo / Jeu); the lead adds lab.lab-patrols card keys. From resources/_template.html: GA4, icons, noindex, ?v=__BUILD__, i18n.js, site.js, bundles, tex.js, lp.js, anim.js (Anim.rng, Anim.colors). MODEL constants: 8 zones, logger gain uncovered R (scaled per correction 7 from 120, 95, 80, 70, 60, 48, 40, 30), caught P (from -40, -40, -35, -35, -30, -30, -25, -25), forest affected if unguarded L = 20, 45, 30, 60, 25, 50, 15, 35 ha; U_a(t,c) = R_t - c_t(R_t - P_t), U_d(t,c) = -(1 - c_t)L_t; m in {2, 3, 4} via the .seg scenario control. ROUTINES (pure): respond(c) returns max U_a, the tie set within 1e-9(1 + |max|), the ranger-favorable and the adverse pick, used for visitor, baselines and optimum alike; sseLP(m, delta) runs 8 LP.solve calls (7 IC rows with b = R_k - R_t - delta, budget row, 8 caps), skips infeasible ones, keeps the best, with delta = 0 and delta = 1; origami(m) by sorted attack-set expansion, asserting equality with sseLP(m, 0) within 1e-6 (console.error otherwise); gridBest(m, step); baselines(m) uniform, top-m by ha, top-m by timber, best deterministic over C(8, m); comb(c, m, u) with normalization and idle segment; replay(D, seed) with Anim.rng. UI: (1) game: canvas park map with 8 stylized zones (fill = forest ha, ring = logger expected gain), 8 sliders at 1% steps under a budget bar clamped to m, 'Loggers decide' pulses the chosen zone in bright red, 3 rounds in a log table, presets 'same patrol every day' and 'spread evenly'; chips ha affected, loggers' expected gain, zones tied at the top, gap to optimum, best reachable with these sliders. (2) 'Show the optimum': water-filling chart (columns from P_t to R_t, line descending to the live water level), 8 mini LP cards with infeasible ones crossed out and the best in --accent plus the note that all share one patrol, the tie-breaking box. (3) 'Tomorrow's patrol': comb strip on [0, m] with m teeth, 'Draw a day' highlights the m zones on the map, 365-day replay with frequency bars, coverage ticks and a 2 SD band. (4) Model card via tex.js: the LP for t* in aligned form, the ERASER MILP, the comb rule. (5) 'What to notice', Further reading (add Korzhyk, Conitzer and Parr 2010), footer note on what is illustrative (map, payoffs, one logger type, identical teams, one zone per team, no travel, loggers know c but not the draw). VERIFY in Python (scipy HiGHS, pulp for the MILP): coverages and water levels, SSE losses 9.764 / 8.159 / 6.761, Z8 LP infeasible only at m = 2, adverse ties 43.66 / 35.43 / 28.26, delta = 1 gives 9.878 / 8.276 / 6.877, rounding sends loggers to Z2, baselines, grid reachable 10.0 / 8.4 / 7.0, MILP equals best LP, comb marginals exact and exactly m zones per day (recompute all after the payoff scaling). Browser checks per CLAUDE.md, including no console errors from the ORIGAMI assert.

shortlist.title_es: Un reparto que ningún grupo rechaza: el núcleo es un PL
shortlist.title_en: A Split No Group Rejects: The Core Is an LP
shortlist.pitch_es: Tres socios comparten recursos y deben repartir lo que ganan, o lo que ahorran, de modo que ningún socio ni ninguna pareja prefiera irse por su lado. Cada coalición resuelve su propio problema de optimización: tres fincas lecheras del valle de Ubaté que convierten la leche que el acopiador no les compra en queso, yogur y arequipe (un PL), o tres productores que comparten un camión (un ruteo exacto). Arrastras tu reparto dentro de un triángulo y se encienden en rojo las coaliciones que lo rechazarían, junto al reparto por precios sombra, el valor de Shapley y el nucléolo. Con el camión pequeño descubres que ningún reparto es estable, y el dual del PL te lo demuestra con un certificado y te dice el subsidio diario que salvaría la alianza.
shortlist.optimization_es: El valor de cada coalición es el óptimo de un PL de producción (o de un ruteo exacto), el núcleo es un poliedro de desigualdades lineales, los precios sombra del PL conjunto dan un reparto dentro del núcleo (teorema de Owen) y el dual de Bondareva y Shapley prueba cuándo el núcleo es vacío y cuánto subsidio hace falta.
shortlist.effort: L (put the nucleolus sequence and the epsilon slider behind details to cut density)
shortlist.strengths: The only cooperative-game candidate: core, Shapley value and nucleolus appear nowhere on the site. Deep, teachable duality story built on Shadow Prices: the Owen split IS the grand coalition's shadow prices; an empty core is certified by the Bondareva-Shapley dual; in the truck case that dual is the LP relaxation of the set-partitioning routing model, so the subsidy (170) is its integrality gap (the cost of stability). Every published number reproduced with HiGHS (labor short v(N) 1,387.1, Owen (400.0, 545.2, 441.9), Shapley (340.0, 676.1, 371.0), nucleolus (339.4, 666.5, 381.3); milk short Shapley blocked by {1,3} and {2,3}; truck 1,118 vs 948). All LPs tiny (at most 6 variables and 9 rows, about 25 LP.solve calls per change). The 'find a split everyone accepts' challenge works as a classroom workshop.
shortlist.risks: Dense: imputation triangle with six lines, four markers, two cases and four scenarios; needs layering and a clear first step. The nucleolus sequence needs extra LPs to decide fixed coalitions, with tolerances. LP.solve assumes x >= 0, so shift variables and split epsilon. Translations must keep core (núcleo, cœur) distinct from nucleolus (nucléolo, nucléole). The truck case as proposed (flower farms trucking to the El Dorado cargo terminal) sits close to the owner's flower pallets paper in preparation and to the Bogotá road maps of Braess and Pricing the Road.
shortlist.corrections: (1) Sign: under max eps s.t. x(S) >= v(S) + eps, the truck 2-loads least-core eps is -113.3; say 'each pair is still 113.3 short'. (2) With an empty core the eps-core appears at eps* = -113.3 as a single point, the nucleolus (all three pair rows tight); it 'shrinks' only in the nonempty cases (to a point in labor short, to a segment in milk short, hence the second LP there). (3) In truck 2 loads every split is blocked, the nucleolus included; compare worst complaints instead: Shapley 141.3 (Madrid + Facatativá pair) vs nucleolus 113.3, the minimum possible. (4) Equal split is not an imputation in either dairy case (labor short 462.4 < v(2) = 545.2; milk short 661 < v(1) = 687.8 and v(3) = 677.4): use the equal-surplus point x_i = v(i) + (v(N) - sum v(i))/3. (5) No Owen point for the truck game (not an LP game): hide that marker and show the integrality-gap reading instead (Göthe-Lundgren, Jörnsten and Värbrand 1996; Bachrach et al. 2009, cost of stability, add to refs). (6) The km table cannot be drawn on a plane (classical MDS has a third positive eigenvalue): use the table as default distances; use 1.3 x straight-line plus a Floyd-Warshall closure only for a farm the visitor drags. (7) Add x_i >= v(i) as hard rows so the sequence computes Schmeidler's nucleolus, not the prenucleolus. (8) Owen sits on the triangle edge in both dairy cases (farm 2 at 545.2 in labor short, farm 1 at 687.8 in milk short); Shapley's violations in milk short are small (6.6 and 2.4 on a surplus of 137.7), so zoom the triangle to the imputation set. (9) Truck 3 loads is a convex game, so Shapley in the core is guaranteed there; do not claim a general theorem about dragging farms. (10) Plausibility: the milk resource is 'surplus milk the collector does not buy (L/day)'; all numbers stay the same. (11) Editor: relabel the truck cargo and destination away from flower exports to El Dorado (keep the verified km table, e.g. three farms sharing a truck to a collection center in another region), to keep distance from the owner's flower pallets paper and from the Bogotá maps of the other road pages.
shortlist.build_plan: Page site/lab/core-is-an-lp.html, bundles site/locales/lab/lab-core.{en,es,pt,fr}.js, prefix core, eyebrow 'Lab · Proposal · Simulation'; the lead adds lab.lab-core card keys. COMPUTE (pure function compute(scenario, data)): (a) dairy A = [[10, 1.1, 2.5], [0.5, 0.1, 0.6], [1, 1, 0]] (rows surplus milk, labor, cold), p = [9, 2.2, 6]; v(S) by LP.solve max with <= rows over pooled b; Owen x_i = y*·b_i; detect a non-unique dual with 6 LPs (min and max y·b_i s.t. A^T y >= p, y >= 0, b_N·y <= v(N) + tol) and draw Owen as a segment when the range exceeds tol. (b) truck: default distances from the km table (0-F 15, 0-M 22, 0-Fa 36, F-M 8, M-Fa 15, F-Fa 22, relabeled per correction 11); optional drag of one farm with 1.3 x straight line and Floyd-Warshall, 'Reset map'; c(S, cap) = min over set partitions within capacity of sum (250 + 6 x best tour); savings v(S) = sum c(i) - c(S); show costs as y_i = c(i) - x_i. (c) core test: LP.solve max sum lambda_S v(S) s.t. sum over S containing i of lambda_S = 1, lambda >= 0 over the 6 proper S; empty iff z > v(N) + tol; certificate lambda, subsidy z - v(N), labeled for the truck as the set-partitioning relaxation and its integrality gap. (d) least core and nucleolus with u_i = x_i - v(i) >= 0 and eps = e+ - e-; per tight free S solve max u(S) with eps fixed (fixed iff <= v(S) + eps + 1e-6 max(1, v(N))); at most 2 stages; keep the stage log. (e) Shapley over 6 orders. (f) triangle: barycentric imputation set, pair lines, core polygon by Sutherland-Hodgman, eps slider for nonempty cores, eps-core appearing at eps* for empty ones. UI (3 columns desktop, stacked on phones with the triangle first): scenario .seg Dairy: labor short / Dairy: milk short / Truck: 3 loads / Truck: 2 loads; case panel (3 farm cards with sliders and Reset, or a schematic SVG map with alliance routes in accent and stand-alone trips in silver); 7-row coalition table with complaint v(S) - x(S) in bright red when positive; SVG triangle with draggable 'Your split' (keyboard arrows), Owen (dairy only), Shapley, nucleolus, equal surplus; HUD chips v(N), saving vs alone, least-core eps (signed), shadow prices or integrality gap, Blocked by; 3-round challenge ending with 'Show proof' (lambda = 1/2 per pair, 678 > 508, subsidy 170); tex.js model card (production LP, set-partitioning c(S), core polytope, Owen theorem, Bondareva-Shapley pair, least-core LP); nucleolus step box in closed details; 'What to notice' with live numbers only; footer note (all data illustrative, town names only). Expected defaults: labor short duals 0.3871 / 8.3871 / 0.9355, eps 60.645; milk short v(N) 1,982.93, Owen (687.80, 485.37, 809.76), nucleolus (701.49, 489.53, 791.90), eps 9.528 then 13.69; truck 3 loads Shapley cost (147.33, 189.33, 357.33), nucleolus cost (175.33, 175.33, 343.33); truck 2 loads c(N) 1,118, relaxation 948, eps -113.33, nucleolus cost (316.67, 316.67, 484.67). VERIFY: independent Python vs page values read in en and es (decimal comma); a farm moved onto the destination makes the 2-load core nonempty; zeroing a farm degenerates the triangle without NaN; 4 languages x 1200 / 700 / 400 px x light and dark, no raw keys, no dashes, no horizontal scroll, formulas render.

shortlist.title_es: Ponle precio a la vía: un juego binivel de peajes
shortlist.title_en: Pricing the Road: A Bilevel Toll Game
shortlist.pitch_es: Manejas una concesión con dos peajes en un corredor ilustrativo de Bogotá hacia Girardot e Ibagué, y los camioneros responden tomando siempre la ruta más barata, incluida una vía libre por el norte. Mueves los dos peajes y ves en un mapa de calor cómo el recaudo cae por precipicios y tiene óptimos locales donde los pasos pequeños se quedan atascados. Luego la página resuelve el problema de dos niveles en forma exacta: lo parte en 16 PL de dos variables y lo convierte en un MILP con condiciones KKT y big M que recorre con ramificación y acotamiento, nodo por nodo. Comparas tu recaudo con el de cobrar cada peaje por separado y con el óptimo, que queda justo donde algún camionero está exactamente indiferente.
shortlist.optimization_es: Es un programa binivel de Stackelberg cuyo seguidor resuelve PL de ruta más barata; con dualidad fuerte y complementariedad con big M se vuelve un solo MILP que se resuelve por ramificación y acotamiento.
shortlist.strengths: The most optimization-heavy candidate: bilevel programming, KKT complementarity, strong duality that linearizes the bilinear revenue, big-M validity and branch and bound with LP.solve, all vocabulary the site already teaches (Inside the Solver, How Big Is M?, the search tree). A real game against the solver. Verified with lp.js: optimum (60, 30) for 153.0 million COP per day vs 90.0 pricing each toll alone (41% less), MILP root bound 156.24, about 30 ms in node; with 80 long-haul trucks the optimum is (60, 60) for 90.0. Goes well beyond Price Wars' smooth closed-form follower.
shortlist.risks: Heavy for undergraduates: put the MILP and B&B in a collapsed 'Under the hood' block. Map plus heatmap plus tree at 400 px. Big-M must be derived from the data. Strong thematic overlap with the Braess page (roads, trucks rerouting, tolls) and methodological overlap with Rangers (one LP per follower response plus a MILP). If built together with Braess, use a clearly different map style and keep this page about revenue-maximizing tolls on uncongested shortest paths.
shortlist.corrections: (1) B&B node count is 25 with best-first on the most fractional z (27 with per-path M), not 17: always compute and print it live. (2) There are 2 x 4 x 2 = 16 pattern LPs (11 feasible), not 64; 4^K is only a general upper bound. (3) Do not call the toll-plane polygons the 'inducible region' (that lives in (t, f) space): 'the toll plane is covered by 16 closed polygons, one per route pattern, and revenue is linear on each'. (4) 'Raising little by little does not work' is false as stated for 800 trucks (a step-1 climb from (0, 0) reaches (60, 30)); climbing gets stuck from the naive (60, 60) and, with 80 trucks, from (0, 0) at (60, 30) with 88.2 vs 90.0. Wording: 'the landscape has cliffs and local optima where small moves get stuck'. (5) 'The optimum always sits on a cliff edge' only when optimal revenue is positive; explain why (otherwise raising a paid toll would raise revenue). At (60, 30) Bogotá to Ibagué trucks face a three-way tie at 470 and Bogotá to Girardot a two-way tie at 290. (6) With 80 long-haul trucks pricing each toll alone is exactly optimal (gap 0); say so; the switch happens at 100 trucks (81,000 + 90 x trucks vs 90,000). (7) Either use Dijkstra with lexicographic labels (cost, then minus toll paid) for the follower or drop the Dijkstra reference. (8) Use a slider-aligned heatmap grid (181 x 181 at step 0.5) and draw region borders as exact lines. (9) Use path flows throughout the notation. (10) Per-path M_p (root bound 154.0) is valid and tighter than per-OD M_k (156.24); prefer it and show both if discussing big-M. Pessimistic followers: revenue 9.0 at (60, 30) vs 152.97 at (59.99, 29.99), the supremum is not attained.
shortlist.build_plan: Page site/lab/pricing-the-road.html, bundles site/locales/lab/lab-tolls.{en,es,pt,fr}.js, prefix toll, eyebrow 'Lab · Proposal · Game'; the lead adds lab.lab-tolls card keys. MODEL: 7 nodes and 11 directed arcs (B-F 120 tolled T1, B-L 170, F-G 110, L-G 120, F-L 60, L-F 60, G-I 150 tolled T2, G-E 70, E-I 140, B-N 200, N-I 270, neutral label 'Norte'); OD demands B-G 1,200, B-I 800 or 80 (scenario .seg), F-I 300; DFS gives 17 paths with cost and toll use; patterns 2, 4, 2. FOLLOWER: minimum cost with optimistic ties (most toll paid), pessimistic toggle in the advanced layer. LIVE: (a) heatmap 181 x 181 at 0.5 cached per scenario; (b) exact region outlines by clipping [0, 90]^2 with the pattern half-planes; (c) 'Price each toll alone' 1D breakpoint scan; (d) 'Ignore detours' (90, 90), revenue 0; (e) 'Climb from here' step-1 hill climb drawn as a trail; (f) 'Solve exactly' 16 two-variable LPs with LP.solve, feasible or infeasible with value, star on the best; (g) 'Let the solver lead' in an 'Under the hood' details block: KKT big-M MILP with 39 variables (t1, t2, pi_1..3, f_1..17, z_1..17), rows demand (3), dual feasibility (17), f_p <= eta_k z_p (17), complementarity with M_p (17), z <= 1 (17), t <= 90 (2), objective max sum eta_k pi_k - sum c_p f_p, best-first B&B with LP.solve in a setTimeout loop, live node count, bound, incumbent, small tree, Inside the Solver style log and the plane region allowed per node; (h) self-check on load: brute force, pattern LPs and MILP agree. UI: map canvas with trucks as dots, arc width by flow, reroutes flashing bright red, MIT red on toll decisions; toll-plane canvas with draggable crosshair linked to two sliders (0 to 90, step 1); chips Revenue, Trucks paying T1, Trucks paying T2, Your best; side by side at 1200 px, stacked at 400 px; final card You vs Price alone vs Climb vs Solver with the gap; bilevel model and single-level MILP via TeX.set; optimum table; 'What to notice'; footer note (corridor, costs, demands and tolls illustrative, no congestion, no real concession). VERIFY in Python (scipy milp with HiGHS): optima for 800 and 80, brute-force grid, 16 pattern LPs with 11 feasible, root bounds 156.24 / 154.0 / 96.62, threshold at 100 trucks, pessimistic values, hill-climb endpoints. Then browser checks per CLAUDE.md with MathJax routed locally.

shortlist.pitch_es: Repartes tus domiciliarios entre cuatro zonas de Bogotá durante diez noches contra una app rival, y en cada zona se queda con los pedidos quien tenga más domiciliarios. Juegas contra un rival que sigue el equilibrio, uno que copia tus repartos o uno codicioso que puedes explotar, y ves que todo reparto fijo tiene un contraataque que lo deja por debajo del valor del juego. Luego una animación muestra cómo el rival encontró su mezcla óptima sin necesitar la matriz completa (286 repartos por bando con 10 domiciliarios): el doble oráculo agrega un reparto a la vez, resuelve un PL pequeño y busca la mejor respuesta con programación dinámica mientras las cotas se cierran como la brecha de un solver. Con 20 domiciliarios en 6 zonas hay 53.130 repartos y el mismo método lo resuelve en vivo.
shortlist.optimization_es: El equilibrio es un PL de suma cero con demasiadas estrategias, y el doble oráculo lo resuelve generando solo las que importan (columnas para un jugador y cortes para el otro) con un subproblema de mejor respuesta resuelto por programación dinámica y cotas que certifican el óptimo.
shortlist.strengths: The best introduction to column and constraint generation with a DP pricing problem and a bound gap that closes like a solver's, an idea absent from the site. Quick and fun on a phone; exploiting the greedy rival and failing to beat the equilibrium rival teaches that no pure plan is safe. Verified with HiGHS and lp.js: values 0 (Even), -2/3 zone (Underdog 8 vs 10), -200 orders (Uneven 8 vs 10); double oracle converges in 20 to 28 iterations in under 25 ms; 20 couriers in 6 zones (53,130 plans) in 72 ms.
shortlist.risks: Its core (a zero-sum game solved as an LP with closing bounds) repeats the penalty page, and the optimization payoff lives only in Act 2. Equilibria are not unique. LP.solve cannot solve the full 286 x 286 matrix (5,000-pivot cap), so the page must never call it on the full game. Visual overlap with Rangers (units over zones). Interactive nights at 400 px need care. Avoid any political framing of Blotto.
shortlist.corrections: (1) '286 by 286' only for Even; with 8 couriers the underdog has 165 plans, so Underdog and Uneven are 165 x 286. (2) 'Too large to write' is overstated for 286 (HiGHS solves it in ms; only lp.js fails): show growth instead (20 in 6 zones: 53,130 plans; 30 in 8: 10,295,472) and say 'the algorithm never needs the full matrix', since the page builds the 286 matrix for the heat map. (3) Uneven zones must be 8 vs 10 (with 10 vs 10 the value is 0 by symmetry). (4) 'No fixed plan is safe' precisely: every fixed plan has a counter that pushes it below the game value (underdog's best fixed plan can be held to -2 zones vs -0.67 with the mix); the strong side with equal zones has a pure plan that never loses on net but gives up 0.67. (5) Against the Equilibrium rival in Even you cannot win on average but do not necessarily lose (146 of 286 plans have expected value 0, e.g. (3,3,2,2)); never say the equilibrium rival beats you. (6) Double oracle generates columns for one player and constraints for the other, not just columns. (7) Iteration counts depend on start and tie rule: compute live, never print 26 / 20 / 26. (8) Label the support and histograms 'this optimal mix' (HiGHS finds 3-plan mixes, double oracle about 17 plans). (9) Stop tolerance about 1e-6 x W (lp.js rounds to 1e-9). (10) Copycat is one-sided fictitious play. (11) Roberson (2006) is the continuous game, background only; add Hart (2008), Discrete Colonel Blotto and General Lotto games, IJGT 36, 441 to 460. (12) Greedy exploitation numbers computed live (Even: (3,3,2,2) loses to (0,4,3,3) by 500 orders; Uneven: (4,3,2,1) loses to (5,0,3,0), a swing of 200).
shortlist.build_plan: Page site/lab/courier-wars.html, bundles site/locales/lab/lab-blotto.{en,es,pt,fr}.js, eyebrow 'Lab · Proposal · Game'; the lead adds lab.lab-blotto card keys. MODEL: 4 zones (Chapinero, Usaquén, Suba, Kennedy); scenario .seg Matchup = Even (10 vs 10, 250 orders per zone) / Underdog (8 vs 10, 250 each) / Uneven (8 vs 10, orders 400 / 300 / 200 / 100); net payoff sum w_k sign(a_k - b_k); captured orders (W + net)/2. ENGINE: enumerate(B, K); solveRestricted via LP.solve with the payoff shifted by W (v = z - W, rival mix = normalized duals, assert sum within 1e-6 of 1); DP oracle per side over zone marginals with a fixed tie rule; doubleOracle from both greedy plans with tol 1e-6 W, logging |R|, |C|, v_t, L_t, U_t, running bounds, new plans and DP tables, precomputed in layout(); 'bigger city' line after first paint (20 in 6 live; 30 in 8 on desktop only). ACT 1 'Ten nights': rival .seg Equilibrium (samples with Anim.rng(seed + night)) / Copycat (greedy night 1, then DP best response to your history) / Greedy; four zone cards with 44 px steppers (2x2 at 400 px), couriers-left counter, Dispatch reveal with pulse and order particles; chips Night, Zones won, Orders captured, Running net, your plan's expected net against the equilibrium and worst case; after night 10 the realized average, expected average, game value and the greedy best reply. ACT 2 'How the rival thinks' (standard player, about 50 s): 1 'Too many plans' (165 x 286 or 286 x 286 heat map from ImageData, growing plan counter); 2 'A tiny game' (restricted matrix grows); 3 'Find a better plan' (DP table lights up, traceback plan enters in bright red); 4 'Bounds close in' (running L and U, gap to 0); 5 'The final mix' (four histograms, plans used, value, 'one of several optimal mixes'). HUD chips iteration, plans used, lower and upper bound, gap, value. tex.js: restricted LP, separable best response, DP recursion, L_t <= v* <= U_t. Footer note on what is illustrative (no app names). VERIFY in Python: full-matrix HiGHS values vs page bounds to 1e-6, DP best response vs brute force on 100 random mixes, no pure saddle point, best-response cycling, greedy numbers, 20 in 6 convergence; node harness on site/assets/lp.js. Playwright per CLAUDE.md plus a 10-night playthrough with each rival.

shortlist.pitch_es: Dos carritos de agua de coco en una playa ilustrativa del Caribe terminan juntos en la mediana de los bañistas, y en una playa uniforme los bañistas caminan el doble de lo necesario. Mueves tu carrito, el computador contesta con su mejor respuesta hasta llegar al equilibrio de Nash, y lo comparas con las ubicaciones que minimizan la caminata total (el problema de 2 medianas). Con tres carritos descubres que ningún arreglo puro es estable: las mejores respuestas dan vueltas para siempre y la página lo prueba revisando las 12.341 ubicaciones posibles. En la última ronda los carritos también fijan precios, huyen a los extremos de la calle y lo resuelves por inducción hacia atrás.
shortlist.optimization_es: Cada jugada es un problema de optimización discreto (maximizar la captura sobre 41 puestos), el equilibrio es un perfil donde todos esos problemas se resuelven a la vez, el planificador resuelve el problema de 2 medianas y la etapa de precios es un problema de complementariedad lineal con matriz definida positiva.
shortlist.strengths: Very playful and inviting, low effort, numerically trivial and exact (prefix sums and enumeration). Teaches existence and nonexistence of pure equilibria, best-response cycles, and the gap between equilibrium and social optimum, with a twist: too little differentiation without prices, too much with prices. Verified: unique 2-cart equilibrium at the center of a uniform beach with walking ratio exactly 2; 0 of 12,341 three-cart placements stable; 12-turn cycle; Round 3 closed form and t/2 at the ends. Connects to One Point, Many Distances (weighted median).
shortlist.risks: The weakest optimization side of the shortlist (enumeration plus a closed form, LP.solve only as an optional certificate that would repeat the penalty page). Best-response dynamics feel close to Price Wars; the Round 3 computer must anticipate the price stage, not act as a Stackelberg leader. Two-peak numbers are not specified and must be computed live. Spots are about 7 px wide at 400 px (step buttons needed).
shortlist.corrections: (1) Say 'a PURE equilibrium may not exist'; a mixed one always exists in this finite game (Nash 1950; continuous version Shaked 1982). (2) The 2-cart equilibrium is unique iff no prefix of bather weight equals exactly W/2: use integer bathers with an ODD total W (an odd number of spots alone is not enough). (3) The 2-median is not unique on the uniform beach ((9,30), (10,30), (10,31) all give 210): show the value and the set of optimal pairs. (4) '1/4 against 1/8 of the beach' is the continuous limit; on 41 spots it is 0.256 and 0.128 of the length (ratio exactly 2). (5) Two-peak numbers (spot 16, 2-median 12 and 32, ratio 2.25) cannot be checked; plausible densities give a median at 14 to 16 and ratios 2.47 to 2.90: compute all live, and say 'together at the weighted median' and 'twice' only for the uniform beach. (6) Round 3 is a two-stage game solved for a subgame perfect equilibrium (EPEC-like), not a bilevel program. (7) Frame the price stage as an LCP with matrix [[2, -1], [-1, 2]] (positive definite, unique price equilibrium) rather than 'KKT'. (8) The closed form assumes inelastic demand and locations in [0, 1]; co-located carts are Bertrand with p = c. (9) Minimum differentiation holds only in the fixed-price game of Rounds 1 and 2; d'Aspremont et al. (1979) showed Hotelling's linear-cost priced version can lack a price equilibrium. (10) Define social cost as bathers' total walking; with a unique equilibrium the price of anarchy is that ratio, otherwise use the worst equilibrium; prefer the label 'walking at equilibrium / planned' and leave formal price of anarchy to Braess. (11) Detect cycles on the state (placement, whose turn); on the grid nonexistence is shown by enumeration, Eaton and Lipsey (1975) is the continuous result. (12) Teach the capture jump at the rival's spot as the reason a continuous best response does not exist.
shortlist.build_plan: Page site/lab/two-carts.html, bundles site/locales/lab/lab-hotelling.{en,es,pt,fr}.js, prefix hot, eyebrow 'Lab · Proposal · Game'; the lead adds lab.lab-hotelling card keys. DATA (declared illustrative): 2 km beach, 41 spots every 50 m, integer two-peak bather profile with an ODD total (e.g. the critic's 631-bather profile adjusted by one), walking speed about 70 m/min; Round 3 uniform 1 km street, c = 2,500 COP, t about 3,000 COP per km^2, every bather buys one unit. ENGINE: prefix sums; capture(carts) in O(1) with exact integer ties (weights x6); best response scanning 41 spots (stay if current spot is a maximizer, else nearest maximizer, then lower index); Nash certificate over 41 deviations per cart; 2-median by 861 pairs cross-checked with an O(N) contiguous split sweep (Hassin and Tamir 1991). ROUND 1 'Two carts': drag or step the red cart, 'Let the computer answer', sand recolored by owner, share bars, move log, 41-bar capture chart with the jump and argmax; declare the equilibrium when both certificates pass; 'Planner's view' with the set of 2-median pairs and the live walking ratio, toggle for the uniform beach (exactly 2). ROUND 2 'Three carts': auto play round-robin best responses, cycle detection on (placement, turn) drawn as a ribbon, 'Check every placement' over 12,341 multisets in setTimeout chunks with progress and '0 stable', showing the improving deviation for the visitor's placement; text 'no pure equilibrium; a mixed one exists'. ROUND 3 'Carts that set prices': prices from the 2x2 LCP, indifferent bather (2 + x1 + x2)/6, computer location best response maximizing reduced profit over 41 spots (backward induction), 41 x 41 reduced-profit heatmap with the equilibrium at the ends (t/2 each vs 0 co-located), planner comparison (quarters give walking t/48 vs t/12 at the ends). Scorecard per round. Model section via tex.js with live values. VERIFY in Python then node: equilibrium set, median, 2-median set by both methods, ratio, 0 three-cart equilibria, cycle period, Round 3 price deviations and grid location equilibrium. Browser checks per CLAUDE.md including keyboard and touch. Add Shaked (1982) and Hassin and Tamir (1991) after checking both citations.

final.recommendation_es: Te recomiendo construir cuatro páginas que cubren cuatro caras distintas de la teoría de juegos sin repetirse entre sí ni con Guerra de precios: Minimax en el punto penal (suma cero, el teorema minimax como dualidad de PL y el aprendizaje que se acerca al equilibrio), El atajo que nos atrasa a todos (congestión, equilibrio como óptimo de un programa convexo y precio de la anarquía), Un reparto que ningún grupo rechaza (juegos cooperativos, núcleo, Shapley y certificados duales) y Los guardaparques juegan primero (Stackelberg: comprometerse con una estrategia aleatoria resolviendo un PL por cada respuesta posible del seguidor). Juntas muestran cuatro herramientas de optimización diferentes: símplex y dualidad, condiciones KKT de un programa convexo, poliedros con precios sombra y certificados, y varios PL para un problema de líder y seguidor. Dos son de esfuerzo M (el atajo y los guardaparques) y dos de esfuerzo L (el penal y el reparto), y todas tienen sus números verificados con las correcciones del crítico ya integradas. Si prefieres un binivel con más optimización (KKT, big M y ramificación y acotamiento), cambia los guardaparques por Ponle precio a la vía, pero entonces la página del atajo debe quedarse en congestión y peajes de costo marginal para no repetir el tema de los peajes. En el caso del camión del reparto conviene cambiar las fincas de flores hacia El Dorado por otra carga y otra región, para no acercarte al artículo de estibas de flores que está en preparación.
also_considered: gt-stable-matching: strong LP link (stable matching polytope with integral vertices) but LP.solve with Bland's rule is near its limit (up to 316 pivots at 6x6, cap hits and fractional answers at 7x7) and the framing against the real rural service (SSO) lottery could read as a critique; good candidate for a later mechanism design round.

gt-shape-of-a-game: elegant map of LP landmarks (security levels, correlated equilibria, Nash bargaining) but animation-only, abstract for visitors, and its mixed-strategy content overlaps the penalty page.
gt-replicator: striking dynamics (spiral, orbit, escape) but the optimization side is the thinnest of the set (ODE and Lyapunov, mirror ascent only conceptual) and there is no hands-on activity.
gt-package-auction: valuable mechanism design (WDP as set packing, VCG as differences of optimal values) but data unspecified, key claims unverified, degenerate LP duals and the largest scope of all.

gt-competitive-location: enumeration-only animation with no visitor choices, seed-dependent headline numbers, and too close to the owner's street markets paper under review (competitive location with logit).

gt-robust-vs-nature: reads as robust optimization more than game theory, overlaps Plan for the Average? and Beyond VaR, and fire base location in an Andean department is too close to the owner's wildfire paper under review.
gt-lemke-howson: mathematically deep (complementary pivoting, odd number of equilibria) but abstract for the audience, custom pivoting code outside LP.solve, near-degenerate data and low engagement.

ranking.title_es: El atajo que nos atrasa a todos
Ponle precio a la vía: un juego binivel de peajes
Un reparto que ningún grupo rechaza: el núcleo es un PL
Plazas estables para el año rural
